doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Learning tunes on the bandstand
summary: He describes sitting in at Manassas with a band and learning songs as they were called.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: What do you do in that situation, or maybe later, if you got on the bandstand and someone calls a tune and everybody knows it but you?

I have several albums from the Manassas Jazz Festival that I recorded and it’s me learning songs. I mean honest to God. Oh you’re so right. Because I was there and a guy, I forget the guy’s name. He led a band called the Red Onion Jazz Band, and he came up to me and he says, “Hey, Allred” he says, “our trombone player’s late getting in, can you do a couple of sets with us.” I said, “Yeah.” And so they’re calling all these tunes, and I knew some, mostly I didn’t. And boy my ears were just like this big and I’m giving it my best shot.
